text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Finnish newspapers this morning.
- Paper Workers' Union chairman Jarmo Lahteenmaki says his union is disappointed with the national pay deal and that it will not join another deal based on the same concept.

- The condition of Helsinki's Meilahti hospital -- Finland's leading specialist hospital -- is the country's worst. Bacteria and humidity jeopardise patients' safety and repairs are done while surgery rooms are in use.
- Unions oppose banks' increased service fees, saying banks have broken earlier promises.
- Owners of some 60,000 cars not in use will have to pay this year's 500 markka atomobile tax.
- Talks between Valmet Automotive, U.S. General Motors and Russian Autovaz on a joint Vyborg based car assembly plant completed, Russian source says.

- Finland's textile industry expects strong growth this year as consumer demand turns from durable goods to semi-durables. Sales of clothes and shoes seen up 4.5 percent, sales of household textiles expected to grow six to eight percent.
- Helsinki telepone company HPY reshuffles managament. Managing director Kurt Nordman to become non-operating president and Matti Mattheiszen to take over as managing director.
- Power producer Imatran Voima (IVO) may look to grow in the UK through acquisitions, new pojects or by expanding services, IVO's UK director John Dean says.
- Finland's Swedish People's Party makes six percent support its official target.
- Conservative Party chairman, Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto says parliament Speaker Riitta Uosukainen suitable as his party's candidate for president.
